key_highlights: US-Iran military strikes trigger oil price spike and broad market selloff across Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq
10-year Treasury yield tops 4.75%, highest since January 2025, signaling rising rate-hike expectations
Kevin Warsh's speech raises bar for Fed to stand pat, reinforcing hawkish bias
Yen breaches 160 level, putting market on intervention watch; Bessent calls moves 'contained'
California wildfire legislation causes PG&E and Edison stocks to plunge
US debt crisis deepens, adding fiscal uncertainty to already stressed rate environment
Crypto (BTC, ETH) pressured lower as rate-hike expectations rise; Saylor restarts $370M Bitcoin buying
Earnings season underway: retailers (BBY, BURL, GAP, ULTA) and tech (MRVL, ESTC, ADSK, PD, S) reporting
Anthropic mega-IPO looms over packed US listing calendar; Enflame seeks $911M IPO in China
Gold sinks on US-Iran strikes despite safe-haven demand; silver also lower on rate expectations
Chile economic reform boosts risk appetite for higher-yield bonds; India absorbs record MSCI flows
Private credit on edge after Australia fiasco; Goldman Sachs sends blunt oil/economy message

sectors.trend: Oil prices jump on US-Iran strikes; LNG exports through Hormuz remain stalled even as oil flows rebound. Goldman Sachs issues blunt oil/economy warning.
sectors.implications: Energy equities and oil-linked commodities benefit short-term; inflation risk rises, pressuring rate-sensitive sectors. Hormuz disruption threatens global LNG supply chains.

sectors.trend: Nvidia's OpenAI investment raises circular financing concerns; Anthropic IPO looms; Marvell, Elastic, Autodesk, PagerDuty, SentinelOne report earnings. XRP nears Nasdaq debut.
sectors.implications: AI capex cycle shows stress signals via circular financing. Earnings quality will determine whether tech rally sustains. Crypto-linked listings (XRP) add regulatory uncertainty.

sectors.trend: PG&E and Edison International plunge on new wildfire legislation imposing stricter liability and cost requirements.
sectors.implications: California utility stocks face structural margin compression. Insurance costs and regulatory overhang create long-term headwinds for regional utilities.

sectors.trend: Best Buy, Burlington, Gap, Ulta report Q2 earnings. Target goes all-in on beauty post-Ulta divorce. Tariff refund handling varies across retailers. Estate sales rise in popularity.
sectors.implications: Consumer spending shows resilience but margin pressure from tariffs persists. Beauty segment consolidation accelerates. Discount retail benefits from cost-conscious consumers.

sectors.trend: 10Y yield at 4.75%; CD rates up to 4.30% APY; mortgage rates elevated; Warsh speech reinforces hawkish stance; US debt crisis worsens.
sectors.implications: Higher-for-longer rates pressure duration-sensitive assets. Banks benefit from net interest margin expansion. Municipal and corporate bond issuance costs rise.

sectors.trend: Chile reform boosts risk appetite; India absorbs record MSCI flows; Adani shares lose $15B; Brazil banks poach hedge-fund talent as industry booms.
sectors.implications: EM divergence continues: policy-positive countries (Chile, India) attract capital while governance concerns (Adani) create volatility. Brazil's private credit boom may be peaking.

sectors.trend: BTC and ETH pressured by rate-hike expectations; Saylor restarts $370M Bitcoin buying; XRP treasury nears Nasdaq listing; TeraWulf CEO sells $2.3M shares.
sectors.implications: Crypto remains rate-sensitive. Corporate accumulation (Saylor) provides floor support. Regulatory progress (XRP Nasdaq) legitimizes sector but adds volatility.

key_themes: Geopolitical escalation (US-Iran strikes) driving oil and risk-off flows
Rising rate expectations (10Y at 4.75%, Warsh hawkish) pressuring growth and crypto
US fiscal deterioration (debt crisis) compounding rate pressure
Yen weakness at 160 triggering intervention risk
Earnings season testing consumer and tech resilience
EM capital rotation toward policy-positive economies
Retail tariff refund divergence and consumer behavior shifts

Reduce USD/JPY long positions; hedge FX exposure; monitor BOJ and Bessent commentary for intervention signals

Scrutinize AI capex quality; favor companies with organic revenue vs. circular funding; monitor OpenAI revenue trajectory
Reduce equity beta into September; increase cash and short-duration bonds; use options for downside protection

market_outlook.short_term: Markets face headwinds from US-Iran escalation, 4.75% 10Y yield, and September seasonality. Expect continued volatility in oil, crypto, and equities. Earnings season (Dell, consumer names, August jobs data) will test resilience. Yen intervention risk adds FX volatility. Net: cautious, range-bound with downside skew.
market_outlook.long_term: If US-Iran conflict de-escalates and Fed holds, equities recover by Q1 2027. Structural themes: AI capex digestion, EM rotation to policy-positive economies, retail consolidation, and energy transition. US debt trajectory remains the dominant macro risk over 6-12 months. Chile and India offer asymmetric upside.
